title: DATE & NUT *laddoos*
name: Date & nut laddoos
intro: No sugar, no fuss. Soft dates hold a handful of toasted nuts together, and ten minutes later you have a box of laddoos for the week.
ingredients: 250 g Zunera Medjool or Kalmi dates, pitted
2 tbsp Zunera pistachios, finely chopped, for rolling
steps: Dry-roast the almonds, cashews and walnuts in a pan over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until they smell toasty. Let them cool, then chop them coarsely.
Blitz the pitted dates in a food processor to a sticky paste, or chop them very finely by hand.
Warm the ghee in the same pan, add the date paste and stir over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until it softens and comes together.
Take the pan off the heat and mix in the chopped nuts and the cardamom.
When it is cool enough to handle, grease your palms with a little ghee and roll the mixture into small balls.
Roll each laddoo in chopped pistachios or coconut. They keep in an airtight box for up to a week.
tip: Soft dates like Medjool and Kalmi bind best. If yours feel dry, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes and pat them dry first.
photoBrief: A plate of date and nut laddoos rolled in green pistachio, a few broken open, on a brass thali with a Zunera pouch behind. Warm side light. Landscape 3:2.

title: KESAR BADAM *milk*
name: Kesar badam milk
intro: Warm saffron milk thickened with almond paste. A cup at bedtime in winter, or chilled on a summer afternoon.
ingredients: A pinch of saffron (8 to 10 strands)
1 to 2 tbsp sugar or jaggery, to taste
steps: Peel the soaked almonds and blend them with 3 to 4 tbsp of the milk to a smooth paste.
Soak the saffron in 1 tbsp of warm milk.
Bring the rest of the milk to a boil, then lower the heat and stir in the almond paste.
Simmer for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring so nothing catches at the bottom.
Add the saffron milk, cardamom and sugar, and simmer for one more minute.
Serve warm, or chill it first, with slivered pistachios on top.
tip: For a silky-smooth drink, pour it through a fine sieve after adding the almond paste.
photoBrief: Two glasses of pale-golden saffron almond milk topped with slivered pistachios and saffron strands, a small bowl of almonds beside. Warm light. Landscape 3:2.

title: DRY FRUIT *kheer*
name: Dry fruit kheer
intro: Slow-cooked rice pudding for festivals and Sunday lunches, finished with cashews and raisins fried golden in ghee.
ingredients: ¼ cup basmati rice, washed and soaked for 20 minutes
steps: Bring the milk to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Add the drained rice and simmer on low heat for 30 to 35 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is soft and the milk has thickened.
Meanwhile, heat the ghee in a small pan. Fry the cashews until golden, add the raisins for a few seconds until they puff up, then set aside.
Stir the sugar, cardamom and saffron into the kheer and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Add the fried cashews and raisins, and the sliced almonds.
Serve warm or chilled, with sliced pistachios on top.
tip: Kheer thickens as it cools. If you are serving it cold, take it off the heat while it still looks a little loose.
photoBrief: A clay bowl of creamy kheer topped with golden cashews, black raisins and sliced pistachios, a brass spoon beside it. Warm light. Landscape 3:2.

title: STUFFED MEDJOOL *dates*
name: Stuffed Medjool dates
intro: The easiest party plate there is. Big, soft dates filled with nut butter, a walnut pressed in and a little chocolate on top.
ingredients: 4 tbsp peanut butter, almond butter or cream cheese
steps: Slit each date lengthwise down one side and take out the seed.
Fill each date with about a teaspoon of nut butter or cream cheese.
Press a walnut half into the filling.
Drizzle with melted chocolate if you are using it, then sprinkle with pistachios and a few flakes of salt.
Chill for 15 minutes to set the chocolate, or serve straight away.
tip: Any soft date works. Try Ajwa or Sukkari Rutab for a smaller, sweeter bite.
photoBrief: Stuffed Medjool dates on a marble board, walnut halves pressed in, chocolate drizzle and green pistachio crumbs. Overhead, natural light. Landscape 3:2.

title: ANJEER *milkshake*
name: Anjeer milkshake
intro: Figs, almonds and a couple of Ajwa dates blended with cold milk. Thick, naturally sweet, and no sugar needed.
steps: Soak the figs and almonds in warm water for 2 hours, or overnight in the fridge.
Drain them, peel the almonds, and chop the figs, cutting off any hard stems.
Blend the figs, almonds and dates with half the milk until smooth.
Add the rest of the milk, the cardamom and the ice, and blend again.
Pour into glasses and top with a little chopped almond.
tip: The dates do the sweetening. Taste before serving and add a third date if you like it sweeter.
photoBrief: Two tall glasses of thick, blush-beige fig milkshake, halved dried figs and a few almonds scattered around. Bright natural light. Landscape 3:2.

title: FIG & WALNUT OVERNIGHT *oats*
name: Fig & walnut overnight oats
intro: Five minutes the night before, and breakfast is waiting in the fridge. Chewy figs and apricots, crunchy walnuts.
ingredients: ½ cup milk, or any plant milk
steps: In a jar, stir together the oats, milk, curd and chia seeds.
Fold in half the chopped figs and apricots.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 6 hours.
In the morning, give it a stir and top with the rest of the fruit, the walnuts and the honey.
tip: The jars keep for 2 days in the fridge, so make a few at once.
photoBrief: A glass jar of overnight oats layered with chopped figs and apricots, walnuts and a drizzle of honey on top, spoon resting on the rim. Morning light. Landscape 3:2.

title: A DATE TASTING *board*
name: A date tasting board
intro: The way dates are served across the Gulf: a few varieties side by side, a pot of coffee, and time to taste the difference.
ingredients: 4 to 5 each of three to five Zunera date varieties, for example:
Zunera Deglet Nour or Mabroom dates, for something lighter and semi-dry
Zunera Sugai or Amber dates, for a mild sweetness
Zunera Khalas dates, for caramel notes
Zunera Sukkari Rutab or Sukkari Mufatal dates, to finish sweet
A small bowl of Zunera in-shell walnuts and a nutcracker
Black coffee or cardamom tea, to serve
steps: Pick three to five varieties. More than five and the differences start to blur.
Arrange them in rows on a board or a large plate, from the lightest and least sweet to the softest and sweetest.
Add the walnuts and nutcracker at one side. A cracked walnut between dates resets the palate.
Brew the coffee or tea and pour small cups.
Taste along the row, one of each, with a sip in between.
tip: Label each row with a small card so guests know what they are tasting. They will want to know which one to buy.
photoBrief: Overhead shot of a wooden board with neat rows of five different dates, from golden to near-black, a bowl of in-shell walnuts and two small cups of coffee. Natural light. Landscape 3:2.

title: CHOCOLATE DATE *truffles*
name: Chocolate date truffles
intro: Three ingredients and a food processor. Soft, dark dates turn into something that tastes far richer than it has any right to.
ingredients: 200 g Zunera Mazafati or Rabia dates, pitted
2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, plus extra for rolling
2 tbsp Zunera pistachios, finely chopped, for rolling
steps: Blitz the almonds in a food processor to coarse crumbs.
Add the dates, cocoa, salt and nut butter, and blitz until it clumps into a dough.
If it feels too dry to hold together, add a teaspoon of water and blitz again.
Roll into small balls with lightly damp hands.
Roll half in cocoa and half in chopped pistachios.
Chill for 30 minutes to firm up. They keep in the fridge for a week.
tip: Mazafati dates are soft and moist, so they bind on their own. With semi-dry dates, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes first.
photoBrief: Chocolate truffles on a small plate, some dusted in cocoa and some rolled in green pistachio, one bitten in half. Dark background, warm light. Landscape 3:2.

title: DATE & WALNUT *cake*
name: Eggless date & walnut cake
intro: The bakery classic, at home. Dates soaked in warm milk give it a soft, toffee-like crumb, and the walnuts give it crunch.
ingredients: 1 cup Zunera Mashrook or Kalmi dates (about 150 g), pitted and chopped
½ cup sugar or brown sugar
1¼ cups whole wheat flour or maida (about 150 g)
½ cup walnuts, roughly chopped (crack Zunera in-shell walnuts, or use Zunera walnut kernels)
steps: Soak the chopped dates in the warm milk for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 180°C and grease and line an 8-inch loaf tin.
Blend the dates and milk with the sugar and oil until smooth.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt.
Pour in the date mixture and fold gently until just combined. Fold in most of the walnuts.
Pour into the tin, scatter the rest of the walnuts on top, and bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool fully before slicing.
tip: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for a few minutes before chopping. It makes a big difference to the flavour.
photoBrief: A loaf of date and walnut cake on a wooden board, two slices cut to show the crumb, walnut halves on top, a cup of chai beside it. Warm light. Landscape 3:2.

title: MUNAKKA *milk*
name: Munakka milk
intro: Seeded black raisins, soaked and simmered in milk. A warm, gently sweet cup that needs no added sugar.
steps: Soak the raisins in a little water for 2 hours, or overnight.
Drain, then slit each raisin and pick out the seeds.
Bring the milk to a simmer with the raisins, almonds, cardamom and saffron.
Simmer on low for 5 minutes, pressing a few raisins against the side of the pan to release their sweetness.
Pour into a cup and drink warm, raisins and all.
tip: Soaking makes the seeds easy to remove and plumps the raisins up so they flavour the milk.
photoBrief: A cup of warm milk with plump black raisins and a few saffron strands, on a wooden table with a small bowl of raisins beside it. Soft evening light. Landscape 3:2.

title: DATE & ORANGE *salad*
name: Date, orange & walnut salad
intro: Sweet, sharp and crunchy. Slices of golden Deglet Nour with orange, toasted walnuts and a honey-lemon dressing.
ingredients: 2 oranges, peeled and cut into segments
8 Zunera Deglet Nour dates, pitted and sliced
¼ cup Zunera walnut kernels, lightly toasted
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper in a small bowl.
Spread the leaves on a plate and arrange the orange segments on top.
Scatter over the sliced dates, the walnuts and the crumbled cheese.
Spoon over the dressing just before serving.
tip: Deglet Nour dates are firm enough to slice neatly, which is why they work so well in salads.
photoBrief: A plate of green leaves with orange segments, sliced golden dates, walnuts and crumbled white cheese, dressing being drizzled on. Bright daylight. Landscape 3:2.

title: HOMEMADE DATE *paste*
name: Homemade date paste
intro: A jar of date paste in the fridge is the easiest swap for sugar. Stir it into chai, oats, smoothies and cake batter.
ingredients: 250 g Zunera Khudri, Fard, Rabbi or Sufri dates, pitted
steps: Put the pitted dates in a bowl and pour over the hot water. Leave for 30 minutes, until soft.
Tip the dates and about half the soaking water into a blender.
Blend until smooth, adding more of the water a spoonful at a time until it is thick but spreadable.
Stir in the lemon juice and spoon into a clean jar.
Keep it in the fridge and use within a week.
tip: Semi-dry dates like Khudri, Fard and Rabbi are ideal here: they soften well and give a thick, rich paste.
photoBrief: A glass jar of smooth, glossy date paste with a spoon in it, a few whole dates beside it on a linen cloth. Soft natural light. Landscape 3:2.
